articles.title: In 2015, Alibaba founder Jack Ma paid $23 million for 28,100 acres in New York’s Adirondacks; he planned to conserve its forests, trout streams and white-tailed deer habitat
articles.summary: US News: In 2015, Alibaba founder Jack Ma purchased the vast Brandon Park estate in New York's Adirondacks for $23 million, focusing on conservation to protect forests, trout streams, and wildlife habitats, while also serving as a personal retreat.
articles.body: In the summer of 2015, a tract of New York's Adirondack wilderness changed hands in a deal that drew attention far beyond the region. Jack Ma, the co-founder of Alibaba, had acquired Brandon Park, a vast private estate of forests, rivers, ponds and wildlife habitat. Unlike a conventional luxury property purchase, Ma's representatives said the land was bought principally for conservation, although he also planned to use it as an occasional retreat. The purchase put a large privately owned landscape under the control of an entrepreneur known for environmental interests in China. It also raised a broader question about the role private ownership can play in conserving landscapes that are valuable for forests, freshwater and wildlife.A vast forest beside the St Regis RiverAccording to the Adirondack Daily Enterprise, Jack Ma paid $23 million for the 28,100-acre Brandon Park estate in Franklin County, in the northwestern Adirondacks. The property included nearly 10 miles of the St. Regis River, trout streams, woodlands and several homes and guest cabins. Other reports on the purchase noted that the estate also contained lakes, ponds, a trout fishery, a horse barn and a maple-syrup operation. The land had a long conservation history before Ma acquired it. Much of Brandon Park had once formed part of a larger private preserve associated with William A. Rockefeller Jr. The Rockefeller family's Adirondack holdings reflected an era when wealthy industrialists established large private estates in the region, often combining hunting and fishing with forest management.By the time Ma bought Brandon Park, however, the property was already part of the larger Adirondack Park, a six-million-acre landscape made up of both public and private land. Ma's purchase did not turn the 28,100 acres into public Forest Preserve land. Instead, the property remained privately owned while its new owner said conservation would be its principal purpose. According to a study published in Landscape and Urban Planning, privately owned working forests and conservation lands form an important part of the Adirondack landscape, and areas perceived as wilderness are not necessarily publicly owned. The research found that some landscapes residents and visitors viewed as wilderness were actually privately managed forests, underscoring the role of private stewardship in preserving the region's undeveloped character.Forests, trout streams and wildlifeBrandon Park’s ecological value came from its forests and waterways. Contemporary reports described the property as containing extensive woodlands, trout waters and habitat for white-tailed deer. Its river frontage, streams, lakes and ponds formed a connected landscape supporting aquatic and terrestrial wildlife.According to research published in the Journal of Wildlife Management, white-tailed deer in the Adirondacks use specific wintering areas where features such as dense conifer cover and watercourses provide suitable conditions. The study highlights the importance of forest structure and landscape features to deer habitat, providing broader ecological context for the type of landscape found at Brandon Park. Rather, keeping a large property relatively undeveloped can help retain existing habitat and maintain ecological connections within a wider landscape.Conservation through private ownershipMa's stated intention was to preserve Brandon Park while retaining the option of using it as a personal retreat. His spokesman said a nonprofit entity would be established to manage the property and described the purchase as Ma's first investment in conservation land outside China.Later reporting in Adirondack Life said the property, then known as New Brandon, was being maintained by local employees and remained connected to Ma's conservation efforts. The magazine also reported Ma's involvement with other international conservation organisations, including the Paradise International Foundation. In that context, the significance of the purchase extends beyond its price to how the property was intended to be managed and conserved.In a region where private land makes up a substantial portion of the Adirondack landscape, the acquisition also illustrates how private ownership can influence the future of large, ecologically connected areas. For Ma, Brandon Park represented both a potential retreat and a conservation project. For the surrounding region, its value lies in the landscape itself: forests along rivers, streams and lakes that support aquatic life, and connected habitats used by wildlife.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: India's GDP growth: BJP hails 'economic resilience'; Congress asks where are the jobs?
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The BJP and Congress on Tuesday traded sharply contrasting assessments of India’s economy after official data showed GDP growth of 7.8 per .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The BJP and Congress on Tuesday traded sharply contrasting assessments of India’s economy after official data showed GDP growth of 7.8 per cent in the April-June 2026 quarter. While the BJP hailed the performance as evidence of resilient economic management, the Opposition questioned whether the growth has translated into jobs, higher incomes and wider prosperity.BJP leader Ravi Shankar Prasad held a press conference where he described the latest growth figures as “particularly significant”. He argued that India had expanded rapidly despite heightened geopolitical and economic uncertainty during the quarter, including the Gulf crisis, disruptions to oil supplies and supply-chain pressures.“Today is a very encouraging day. The latest report shows that India’s GDP growth stood at 7.8 per cent in the April-June 2026 quarter. The figure of 7.8 per cent is particularly significant because, during this period, the Gulf crisis had intensified. There were concerns over oil supplies, disruptions in supply chains, and uncertainty across the global economy. Despite all these challenges, India’s economy grew by 7.8 per cent,” Prasad said at a press conference in Delhi.Prasad also compared India’s performance with growth recorded by several other major economies, saying Canada grew by around 1.5 per cent, Germany by 1 per cent, the UK by 2.1 per cent, Malaysia by about 6 per cent, South Korea by around 3.7 per cent and the US by roughly 2 per cent during the same period.He attributed India’s performance to what he called effective economic management and praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership.“Today, I would like to congratulate and commend India’s economic management. I also wholeheartedly congratulate the honourable Prime Minister for his vision, wisdom and leadership,” Prasad said.The Congress, however, challenged the BJP’s interpretation of the GDP figures, arguing that headline growth alone does not adequately capture the economic conditions faced by ordinary Indians.Congress leader Pawan Khera questioned how the 7.8 per cent growth figure was benefiting young people and farmers, while also pointing to concerns over employment, manufacturing, education and income distribution.“The Prime Minister comes up with a reel, a video. Ask him: the largest demographic in this country is the youth. How does this GDP growth affect the youth? How does it address the issues that young people face? The largest occupation in this country is agriculture. How does this GDP growth affect the agricultural sector? If it doesn’t benefit these two sectors, how does it affect the dwindling manufacturing sector? Look at the manufacturing data. So, what is he even talking about? A handful of people contribute to the growth of this country, but where is the redistribution of income? Where is the distribution of income? So, let’s talk about these fundamental issues. 80 per cent of this country depends on free ration. Is that what good GDP growth does for the country? That’s our question.”Khera had earlier taken his criticism to X, arguing that a single quarter of strong GDP growth should not be treated as evidence of broad-based economic prosperity.“One quarter of 7.8% growth is not an economic spring. If India has truly "bloomed," why do rampant unemployment, leaked exam papers, and a crumbling education system define the ground reality? Why is the republic's prosperity not translating into the prosperity of its public? GDP measures national output - not jobs, not wages, not opportunity. If it measured any of those, the future of India's youth would not look so bleak. Modi can manage his headlines. For India's youth, the question remains the same as ever: Where are the jobs?”At his press conference, Khera also questioned whether the strong GDP reading had resulted in tangible improvements in the cost of living and employment conditions.“On one hand, they say, "Look at the GDP of a single quarter and applaud." On the other, they say, "Don't buy gold, don't host lavish weddings." They themselves sit abroad while telling the country's citizens not to travel overseas and to save money. 80% of the population relies on free rations, but keep applauding... Regarding this 7.8% figure—what benefit is the country's largest sector, agriculture, deriving from it? The youth constitute the country's largest demographic; what benefit are they getting? Have their issues been resolved? Have milk prices dropped? Is there no longer a need for free rations? Have you rectified the employment situation to reverse the 45-year record low? Is manufacturing back on track? What happened to the MSME sector? What happened to the unorganized sector? If you have answers showing a positive outcome, then we, too, will applaud...”The competing responses underline the political divide over how India's economic performance should be assessed. While the BJP has used the 7.8 per cent quarterly expansion to highlight India's relative resilience amid global disruptions, the Congress has focused on whether headline GDP growth is being reflected in employment, household incomes and opportunities for India's young population.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Quote of the day by Princess Diana: "I like to be a free spirit. Some don't like that, but…" - powerful words on being yourself
articles.summary: UK News: Princess Diana's words reflect her genuinely independent nature and her willingness to remain true to herself, even when doing so clearly stood apart .
articles.body: Princess Diana's words reflect her genuinely independent nature and her willingness to remain true to herself, even when doing so clearly stood apart from what was expected of her public role. "I like to be a free spirit," she said. "Some don't like that, but that's the way I am." Diana became one of the most recognisable members of the British royal family, and her genuine popularity was closely connected to the way she presented herself as approachable and human, often following her own instincts rather than the formal expectations traditionally associated with royal life. Her words carry a genuinely simple message about being yourself, accepting real criticism, and having the confidence to live honestly according to your own actual personality, a lesson that showed up in her public life in ways considerably more visible than a single quote ever could.Quote of the day by Princess Diana"I like to be a free spirit. Some don't like that, but that's the way I am"A real moment that captured this exact ideaOne of the clearest real examples of Diana's independence came through fashion rather than words. In 1994, she wore a striking black off-the-shoulder dress designed by Christina Stambolian to a public event, on the very same evening that Prince Charles publicly admitted adultery on television. The dress became widely known afterwards as the "revenge dress," and it was understood at the time as a deliberate, quiet statement made entirely on her own terms, a genuinely visible way of showing the public that she remained confident and independent regardless of what was happening around her privately. That single evening captured something real about the personality behind today's quote, someone willing to be seen exactly as she actually was, rather than as anyone else expected her to present herself.The deeper meaning of Princess Diana’s quoteDiana's words suggest that she genuinely valued her own freedom to actually be herself, even at moments when other people clearly did not approve. Being a "free spirit" can mean having a genuinely independent personality, following your own instincts, and refusing to let other people's expectations completely determine how you behave. The second half of the quote matters just as much as the first. Diana acknowledges honestly that some people may genuinely dislike her nature, yet she never suggests that their disapproval should actually change who she is underneath it all.Why simply being yourself can genuinely be difficultBeing authentic sounds genuinely simple in theory, yet it becomes considerably harder once people are constantly watching or judging you, exactly as Diana experienced throughout her adult life. Real expectations from family, colleagues or wider society can influence how people actually behave, creating genuine pressure to fit in, avoid criticism, or behave in ways that simply make other people comfortable. Diana's quote suggests that real individuality sometimes requires honestly accepting that not everyone will ever genuinely approve of you.Princess Diana's public life faced genuinely intense scrutinyDiana entered the British royal family at a genuinely young age and quickly became one of the most photographed people in the entire world. Her clothing, her relationships and her personal life were frequently discussed across the media, and living under that level of attention made complete privacy almost impossible to maintain. Yet she developed a genuinely distinctive public personality regardless, often appearing considerably more relaxed and spontaneous than the formal image traditionally associated with royal life before her.How Diana actually expressed her individualityDiana became known specifically for the way she interacted directly with people. She was often photographed speaking closely with members of the public during her charitable work, famously abandoning the formal royal protocol of wearing gloves so she could actually touch the people she met. Her approach helped create a genuine image of a royal figure willing to step outside traditional convention, and that individuality became a genuine part of her lasting public appeal.Being genuinely independent never actually meant ignoring everyone elseBeing a free spirit does not necessarily mean refusing all advice or simply doing whatever you want regardless of consequence. Healthy independence involves making your own real decisions while still genuinely understanding that other people may hold different opinions. Diana's quote recognises this reality honestly. She knew that some people would never actually approve of her personality, yet she remained comfortable enough with herself not to let every single piece of criticism determine her actual behaviour.Why fear of criticism can genuinely make people hide their true personalityA real fear of judgement can encourage people to quietly change themselves purely to fit outside expectation. Someone might avoid expressing a genuine opinion or pursuing a real interest simply because they are worried about how others will actually react to it. Over time, constantly seeking outside approval can make it genuinely difficult to even know what you actually want anymore. Diana's words offer a genuinely different approach instead, accepting honestly that criticism exists without letting it completely control your own identity.The real importance of accepting that not everyone will like youTrying to be liked by absolutely everyone is genuinely impossible. Different people hold different values, personalities and real expectations, and a decision that one person genuinely admires may frustrate someone else entirely. Accepting this honestly can make it considerably easier to actually live with real confidence, while also spending considerably less energy trying to satisfy every single outside opinion that comes your way.Other memorable quotes by Princess Diana"When you are happy you can forgive a great deal.""I don't go by the rule book… I lead from the heart, not the head.""Anywhere I see suffering, that is where I want to be, doing what I can.""If you find someone you love in your life, then hang on to that love."How to embrace Princess Diana's lessonKnow yourself genuinely, understanding your own values, interests and personality honestly.Accept real disagreement, since someone disliking your choices does not automatically mean they are actually right.Do not live entirely for outside approval, since constantly seeking validation can make you lose sight of what you genuinely want.Stay open to genuinely useful criticism, since being independent has never actually meant refusing to learn.Make your own real decisions, taking honest responsibility for the choices that actually shape your life.Protect your own individuality, remembering you never actually have to copy everyone around you.Be genuinely comfortable being different, since standing apart can sometimes become a real strength.Set healthy boundaries, respecting other people's opinions without letting them actually control you.Follow your real interests, giving yourself genuine permission to explore what actually matters to you.Stay authentic, letting your actions honestly reflect who you actually are underneath it all.Why Princess Diana's quote remains relevantDiana's words capture a genuine tension that a great many people experience, the desire to be themselves while also genuinely wanting to be accepted by others around them. Her message was never that criticism should always be ignored entirely. It suggests instead that a person's real identity should never be completely shaped by other people's approval alone. Being yourself can sometimes genuinely mean disappointing people, challenging outside expectation, or choosing a path that others simply do not understand. Diana's own description of herself as a "free spirit" reflects that genuine willingness to remain individual despite real outside judgement. You cannot actually control whether everyone genuinely likes who you are. You can, however, genuinely choose whether their opinions ultimately determine who you become.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: About 20 years ago, Dawn Robinson paid $40,000 for 2.4 acres in New Jersey; Middle Township later offered her $47,000 and is now trying to take the land for a 340-home project
articles.summary: US News: In South Jersey's Middle Township, a war goes on. The township has filed an eminent domain condemnation complaint that seeks to acquire 2.4 acres of l.
articles.body: In South Jersey's Middle Township, a war goes on. The township has filed an eminent domain condemnation complaint that seeks to acquire 2.4 acres of land in Whitesboro for a large-scale housing development project. But the woman who owns the property, Dawn Robinson, does not want to give it up, according to a report by WHYY.“The land is already paid for,” Robinson said. “If I wanted to sell, I would have had a ‘for sale’ sign on it. I’m not being rude, I don’t want to sell. I want to keep it for my kids.”An eminent domainWhat does eminent domain mean? Well, an eminent domain gives the government the power to take away someone's private property. However, the Fifth Amendment states a property may only be taken away if it is for public use and the owner is paid just compensation.Middle Township wants to take her land in order to move forward with a multi-million dollar housing development plan, known as the Indian Trail Redevelopment project, to be built by a private, for-profit developer, NVR, Inc, also known as Ryan Homes. A show-cause hearing on the matter that was scheduled for May 6 was postponed until July 1. At a second court appearance in July, Robinson agreed to attend a mediation session to try to negotiate a land-swap settlement, but no deal was reached during the closed-door session, so the case could soon head back to court.Robinson hopes to convince a judge the housing development plan on the table doesn’t need to include her property. “I would love to keep my land and develop it myself,” she said. “I bought this land from the township, they didn’t tell me there was an expiration on it.”“They could build around me, no problem,” she added. She stressed that her property is on the outer edge of where the developer wants to build the housing project.Robinson shared that nine years ago, an attempt was made to force the acquisition of dozens of parcels of land using eminent domain, but a judge rejected the proposal and the redevelopment of the area stalled.Kerrin Wolf, an associate law professor at Stockton University, said that if a town uses eminent domain, there needs to be a specific plan in place to redevelop the area in question. “They use [eminent domain] sometimes to build schools, sometimes to expand roadways, sometimes for public-private partnerships,” Wolf said.Eminent domain can be used for commercial developments, as long as officials can prove the project is for legitimate public use. “They have to show that the development will be good for the community in some significant way, you have to have a very specific plan that shows clear public good,” he said.“Eminent domain is supposed to be for public use,” said Robinson. “Everyone knows that is not happening in this case.” She pointed out that last month the New Jersey Supreme Court issued a unanimous decision in Jackson Township v. Getzel Bee. In that case, the court ruled that local governments cannot use eminent domain to condemn private land and then transfer it to a developer.Affordable housing on the other sideMiddle Township Mayor Christopher Leusner has strongly supported efforts to move the project forward, calling it “a transformative initiative” that will bolster township services. He said in a statement that the 340-home project “will deliver much-needed housing, help fulfil the township’s affordable housing obligations, generate millions in new revenue for the township and convert long-vacant, fragmented land into a vibrant residential community.”James Maley, a partner at the law firm Maley Givens in Collingswood, said his firm will represent Middle Township in the condemnation proceeding. He said the lots being taken are extremely small and were given to people in the 1930s as part of a newspaper promotion.“The township has been working for 10 years on assembling lots so that [the property] can be developed,” Maley said. “A development of this nature is critical for the community to provide more opportunities for decent housing. It will also increase the [township’s] ratable base and make the township more affordable for everyone.”Maley said affordable housing units will be offered as part of the project, and that dozens of lots have already been acquired in preparation for the development to move forward.Help from outsideRobinson's friend, Janice Roots, helped convince the co-founders of Truth and Record, an online platform that advocates for social justice and accountability, to help spread the word about her case and collect donations for her legal defence. “They work on behalf of the descendants of those sold as enslaved people,” Roots said. “They have a strong network throughout the country, and I felt they would be a good resource.”Roots said she felt compelled to help Robinson for personal reasons. “My family has been through the exact same situation,” she said. “My great-great-grandfather received 40 acres after emancipation around 1870. Subsequently, the land was seized from him, and I didn’t want to see history repeat itself with Dawn.”Rachel Davis, the co-founder of Truth and Record said they decided to help Robinson since they felt it was an "unjust case." “Eminent domain is often used by the government to displace predominantly Black and Brown people and poor people, and our stories that we tell come from that historical perspective.”Truth and Record’s other co-founder Chelsea Nicolas said the case raises several red flags. “This case is located in a historically Black neighbourhood, and eminent domain is being used to seize land for a private developer, she said. “The significance of this on economic security, inheritance, community continuity, all of those things are impacted.”She said a website has been established to help collect donations for Robinson’s legal costs and to tell her story. Robinson said she feels honoured that people in her community and others she doesn’t even know are helping her.“I think my neighbours believe that if it happens to me, it can happen to them, with eminent domain, that they can just take your ownership from you if they want your land,” she said.Robinson said even if she wanted to sell, part of the legal agreement she has been offered stipulates that if the land ever needs to be remediated, she would be financially responsible for whatever needed to be done, even after the sale was complete. “If they find anything on it, tomorrow or 20 years from now, I’m responsible for that,” Robinson said. “How can they take something from me and hold me responsible?”Robinson said she has been offered $47,000 for her 2.4-acre property, which is right next to her current home. However, that is only $7,000 more than what she initially paid for the property 23 years ago. She said she originally owned two lots, but that the township split one of them in half, so technically, she is now the owner of three parcels of land.If an agreement is not reached, the case will head back to Superior Court at an unspecified date for a final judgment on whether the township has the authority to take Robinson’s property. If the eminent domain complaint is upheld, a three-person commission would then decide the value of her 2.4 acres.“I’m not in the way,” she said. “I really can’t say they need [my property], I feel it’s more that they just want it.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
